- The patient presented with symptoms of chronic fatigue, dizziness, headaches, and cognitive slowing following recent psychological trauma and a preexisting mood disorder, prompting evaluation for systemic and neurological contributions [[1]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb26f25724764f6fbb0ffe).
- Diagnoses identified mild anemia, elevated inflammatory markers, and a CT scan of the brain showing mild cortical atrophy in frontal and temporal lobes, with no acute hemorrhage, infarct, or mass lesion [[1]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb26f25724764f6fbb0ffe).
- Pathology and imaging results completed on 27/06/2025 showed hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL (mildly low), hematocrit 34% (low), WBC count 9.6 x10^3/uL (normal), CRP (hs) 4.8 mg/L (elevated), and ferritin 25 ng/mL (borderline low) [[2]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb26f25724764f6fbb0ffe).
- The patient was continued on an inhaled vaporised THC flower (25%THC, <1%CBD) for ongoing pain, insomnia, and anxiety management [[3]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- The patient was continued on a CBD 100mg/ml oil Cat1 for ongoing pain, insomnia, and anxiety management [[3]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- The pre-operative diagnosis was to rule out systemic inflammation, anemia, and neurological abnormalities related to depressive symptoms [[1]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb26f25724764f6fbb0ffe).
- The mild cortical atrophy observed on the CT scan is considered possibly stress-induced or representing early neurodegenerative changes [[1]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb26f25724764f6fbb0ffe).
- On last review, the patient was receiving good therapeutic benefit from medicinal cannabis with minimal side effects or adverse reactions, which has reduced her need for further medications [[3]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- Consent limitations and risks associated with medicinal cannabis use were discussed, and the patient is aware not to drive at any time when using any product containing THC [[3]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- Dietary and lifestyle adjustments were recommended to address anemia [[2]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb26f25724764f6fbb0ffe).
- Psychiatric evaluation was recommended for cognitive decline [[2]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb26f25724764f6fbb0ffe).
- Neurology referral was recommended for follow-up imaging and cognitive testing in 6 months [[2]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb26f25724764f6fbb0ffe).
- Antidepressant and anti-inflammatory intervention was suggested for consideration based on full clinical correlation [[2]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb26f25724764f6fbb0ffe).

PRE-OPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: Rule out systemic inflammation, anemia, and neurological abnormalities related to depressive symptoms.

DIAGNOSIS: Mild anemia and elevated inflammatory markers identified. CT scan of the brain reveals mild cortical atrophy, possibly stress-induced or early neurodegenerative changes. No acute hemorrhage or mass lesion observed.

NOTE: Recommend dietary and lifestyle adjustments to address anemia. Psychiatric evaluation for cognitive decline. Neurology referral for follow-up imaging and cognitive testing in 6 months. Consider antidepressant and anti-inflammatory intervention based on full clinical correlation.

**Discussion**
- The consultation was conducted via telehealth to assess suitability for continued use of medicinal cannabis for chronic back pain, ankle pain, anxiety, and insomnia symptoms [[1]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- The patient sustained chronic back pain following multiple epidural procedures and gastrocnemius tendon pain from an injury that required surgical management [[2]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- The patient previously trialled various analgesics and anti-inflammatory medications that produced either suboptimal therapeutic effect or intolerable side effects [[2]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005)[[3]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- Prior to the consult, the patient was prescribed a combination of oral slow- and fast-release CBD and THC products with good therapeutic benefit [[2]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- The patient denied illicit cannabis use, reported no side effects or adverse events from prescribed phytocannabinoids or THC, and had no alerts on SafeScript or evidence of drug-seeking behaviour [[2]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005)[[4]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- The patient denied current unstable cardiovascular disease, arrhythmia, personal history of psychotic disorder or acute psychosis, other unstable psychiatric conditions, or anticoagulant use [[5]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- The patient was not managed by a psychiatrist or specialist at the time of review, and denied pregnancy, breastfeeding, or plans to conceive [[3]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005)[[5]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- The patient has no known allergies [[1]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).

**Findings**
- On examination, the patient was pleasant, polite, and cooperative [[3]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- No primary contraindications or precautions to continuing inhaled or oral slow-release cannabinoids were identified [[4]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- The record does not contain vital signs or physical examination findings.

**Assessment**
- Refractory chronic pain secondary to prior injury and epidural procedures, associated with ongoing anxiety and sleep disturbances, with sustained benefit from cannabinoid therapy [[1]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005)[[5]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).

**Plan**
- Continued on inhaled vaporised THC flower (25% THC, <1% CBD) for pain, insomnia, and anxiety management [[3]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- Continued on CBD 100 mg/mL oil Cat1 for pain, insomnia, and anxiety management [[3]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- Limitations and risks of medicinal cannabis discussed, and the patient was advised not to drive at any time when using THC-containing products [[3]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
- Patient agreed to consult with her regular GP to monitor for any necessary medication adjustments [[5]](https://clinic.asksam.com.au/clinical/home?view=view&noteType=Follow-up&clinicalId=6adb50e45724764f6fbb1005).
